activity_context.topic_title: Representing 2x2 Systems of Equations Using a Matrix Product

examples.knowledge_point: Representing a 2x2 System of Equations Using a Matrix Product by Reorganizing
examples.problem:
Represent the following system of equations using matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-5y=-3x \\ 6+x=-2+y\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we organize the system so that it’s in the correct order:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}3x-5y=0 \\ x-y=-8.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b},$ where

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052302/assets/648952bc6e093c08ff29215fce21fe115ab81e9fc3d8b423772123eae31237f3.png)

is the coefficient matrix,

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052302/assets/c1f203be0770c298d9c2c75ccfbfb30354cb314ed75c8b05f6639e5633ca7442.png)

is the column vector of constants, and

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052302/assets/aa4de061ca95088763e7e5fec289dbd2e5bd298e8986ef6660617ea0ba227821.png)

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$ becomes

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052302/assets/75aed8c54a2ec274def967802cbd3b67d0fad3358e676b02cf52e1e8d2cbe0d7.png)

feedback.problem:
Represent the following system of equations using matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-2x+5y=-1 \\ 5x=15\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that both $x$ and $y$ appear in each equation. 
The variable $y$ does not appear in the second equation, but this just means its coefficient is $0.$ So, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-2x+5y=-1 \\ 5x+0y=15\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 15\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 15\end{aligned}].
$$
